items.text: The system shall let the user select a specific park so that subsequent ticketing and add-on content is localized to that park.

claims.claim: The flow exposes a park-selection mechanism with park options.
A specific park can be selected as the active park context.
Later ticketing or add-on pages are localized to the selected park.

items.evidence_note: Steps 1-3 show park selection ending in Six Flags America; later purchase pages and the cart retain that park context.
items.rationale: All observable core claims are supported by the ordered flow.

items.text: The system shall present park-specific passes and in-park purchase options after a park has been selected.
items.annotation_notes: The visible flow supports park-specific purchase content after the park has been selected.

claims.claim: After park selection, the homepage displays the selected park context.
Park-specific pass or in-park purchase options are presented after selection.

items.evidence_note: Step 4 shows Six Flags America with pass merchandising; step 6 shows season add-ons for the purchase flow.
items.rationale: The visible flow supports park-specific purchase content after the park has been selected.

items.text: The system shall support navigation from a park homepage into add-on purchasing sections associated with tickets or passes.
items.annotation_notes: The sequence moves from the localized park page into a dedicated season add-ons view, showing that add-on shopping is reachable from the park-level browsing context.

claims.claim: The park homepage exposes navigation related to tickets, passes, or add-ons.
The flow reaches an add-on purchasing section from that park browsing context.

items.evidence_note: The localized homepage and tickets menu lead to the Season Add-Ons page.
items.rationale: The required navigation outcome is visibly shown.

items.text: The system shall present optional add-on plans with enough descriptive and pricing information for users to compare them before selection.
items.annotation_notes: The visible cards provide enough basic title, description, and price information for comparison.

claims.claim: Multiple optional add-on plans are presented before selection.
The add-on options include visible descriptive information.
The add-on options include visible prices or starting prices.

items.evidence_note: Step 6 shows add-on cards for Flash Pass, Dining Pass, Go-Karts, and Season Drink Bottle with descriptions and prices.
items.rationale: The visible cards provide enough basic title, description, and price information for comparison.

items.text: The system shall support category-based browsing of purchasable items within the ticketing and add-on shopping interface.
items.annotation_notes: The category-based shopping interface is visibly present and contains purchasable items.

claims.claim: The shopping interface exposes product categories or tabs.
Purchasable items are browsed within the selected category interface.

items.evidence_note: The modal contains category tabs such as Daily Tickets, Season Passes, THE FLASH PASS, Group Tickets, Dining, More Deals, and Promo.
items.rationale: The category-based shopping interface is visibly present and contains purchasable items.

items.text: The system shall allow the user to choose among multiple add-on variants within the selected park context.
items.annotation_notes: The user can visibly choose among more than one add-on variant.

claims.claim: The selected park context remains visible while add-on shopping is open.
The add-on interface offers multiple add-on variants to choose from.

items.evidence_note: Step 7 shows two go-kart product variants while the Six Flags America context remains in the page chrome.
items.rationale: The user can visibly choose among more than one add-on variant.

items.text: The system shall present an itemized pre-checkout order summary including subtotal, fees, tax, and total.

claims.claim: The cart review shows itemized line items before checkout.
The pre-checkout summary shows subtotal, fees, tax, and total.

items.evidence_note: Step 10 shows line items plus Subtotal, Processing Fee, Tax, and Total.
items.rationale: The required pricing summary is visibly present before checkout.

items.text: The system shall provide a dedicated detail view for a selected add-on before it is added to the cart.
items.annotation_notes: The dedicated view appears before cart addition.

claims.claim: Selecting an add-on opens a dedicated detail or configuration view.
The item is not added immediately before the user reviews the detail view.

items.evidence_note: Step 8 shows a product detail/configuration panel for the 2023 All Season Go-Kart Pass with Back and Add to Cart actions.
items.rationale: The dedicated view appears before cart addition.

items.text: The system shall disclose important product conditions such as eligibility, usage restrictions, or special purchase notes before the user commits to an add-on purchase.
items.annotation_notes: The flow shows visible product notes such as membership-related conditions and ride restrictions. The disclosure is visible, while actual enforcement would depend on hidden logic.

claims.claim: The add-on purchase flow discloses eligibility or purchase conditions before the user commits to the add-on.
claims.note: tep 6 states the All Season Go-Kart Pass is “Only available to Pass and Legacy Membership Holders.” Step 8 repeats the Go-Kart add-on detail before Add to Cart.

claims.claim: The add-on purchase flow discloses usage or safety restrictions before the user commits to the add-on.
claims.note: Step 8 shows height requirements, driving requirement, medical/safety restrictions, and availability/weather limitations before the Add to Cart button.

items.evidence_note: Step 6 notes pass or legacy membership availability for go-karts, and step 8 shows ride and safety restrictions before Add to Cart.
items.rationale: Visible disclosure is supported, but screenshots cannot establish that every important condition is disclosed or enforced.

items.text: The system shall allow the user to adjust add-on quantity before adding the selected item to the cart.
items.annotation_notes: The add-on detail view includes quantity controls, and the next screen shows the quantity increased from one to two before cart addition.

claims.claim: The add-on detail view provides quantity controls before Add to Cart.
The pending add-on quantity can change before Add to Cart.

items.evidence_note: The quantity control is visible at quantity 1 in step 8 and quantity 2 in step 9.
items.rationale: The visible state change supports quantity adjustment before cart addition.

items.text: The system shall let the user cancel an add-on configuration step without losing the broader shopping context.
items.annotation_notes: A Back action is present inside the add-on configuration modal, suggesting the user can retreat without abandoning the overall purchasing flow.

claims.claim: The add-on configuration view provides a visible way to back out or cancel the configuration step.
Using that action returns to the broader shopping context without losing it.

items.evidence_note: A Back button is visible in the configuration modal, but the flow does not show it being used.
items.rationale: The mechanism is visible, but the outcome of backing out without losing context is not shown.

items.text: The system shall add configured add-ons to the shopping cart and reflect the selected quantity in cart line items.

claims.claim: The configured add-on quantity is reflected before the add-on is added to the cart.
The shopping cart contains the configured add-on as a line item.
The cart line item reflects the selected quantity.

items.evidence_note: Step 9 shows quantity 2 for the go-kart pass, and step 10 shows the All Season Go-Kart Pass line with Qty 2.
items.rationale: The visible cart line item confirms the configured add-on and selected quantity.

items.text: The system shall support carts that combine admission products with optional add-ons in a single order review.

claims.claim: The cart review contains an admission product.
The same cart review contains an optional add-on product.

items.evidence_note: Step 10 shows a One-Day Ticket and a 2023 All Season Go-Kart Pass in the same shopping cart.
items.rationale: The cart visibly combines admission and add-on products in one order review.

items.text: The system shall preserve the selected park context consistently across discovery, add-on selection, and cart review screens.

claims.claim: The selected park context is visible during discovery or homepage browsing.
The selected park context remains visible or referenced during add-on selection.
The selected park context remains visible or referenced during cart review.

items.evidence_note: Six Flags America is shown after park selection and the cart acknowledgment references Six Flags America, Baltimore, Maryland/Washington.
items.rationale: The visible screens consistently preserve the selected park context; hidden session implementation is treated as a routine dependency.

items.text: The system shall allow cart contents to be reviewed and modified before proceeding to checkout.

claims.claim: The cart contents can be reviewed before checkout.
The cart review provides a visible modification mechanism before checkout.

items.evidence_note: Step 10 shows a cart review with a Modify Cart action and Checkout still ahead.
items.rationale: The visible cart state supports review and modification before proceeding.

items.text: The system shall distinguish optional marketing consent from required purchase acknowledgements during the transition to checkout.
items.annotation_notes: The separation is visible, but enforcement of required purchase acknowledgement is not directly demonstrated.

claims.claim: Marketing consent is distinguished as a separate optional opt-in.
Purchase acknowledgements are shown separately from the marketing opt-in.
The requiredness of the purchase acknowledgement depends on enforcement behavior.
claims.note: The checkout button is disabled, since the purchase acknowledgement isn't consented yet.

items.evidence_note: Step 10 separates a marketing/news checkbox from a purchase terms checkbox; the marketing text states it is not a condition of purchase.
items.rationale: The separation is visible, but enforcement of required purchase acknowledgement is not directly demonstrated.

items.text: The system shall provide accessibility support such as a high-contrast viewing mode during the purchase workflow.

claims.claim: A high-contrast accessibility control is visible during the purchase workflow.

items.evidence_note: The purchase modal and cart review show a High Contrast Mode control.
items.rationale: A visible accessibility support mechanism is present during the purchase workflow.

items.text: The system shall support selection of a digital or mobile ticket fulfillment option as part of the purchase flow.
items.annotation_notes: The task explicitly mentions choosing a digital ticket option, and the visible flow reaches cart review where delivery or fulfillment choices commonly appear, but the explicit control is not clearly shown in the provided screenshots.

claims.claim: The system provides a control for choosing a digital or mobile ticket fulfillment option.
The chosen digital or mobile ticket option is reflected later in the purchase flow.

items.evidence_note: The cart review is visible, but no explicit digital or mobile ticket fulfillment selector or selected fulfillment state is shown.
items.rationale: The screenshots do not provide enough visible evidence to verify or contradict fulfillment-option support.

items.text: The system shall provide visible feedback when the selected quantity changes so the pending purchase configuration remains clear.
items.annotation_notes: The quantity change is reflected in the pending purchase configuration before cart addition.

claims.claim: The system provides feedback when the selected quantity changes.
The pending purchase configuration remains clear after the selected quantity changes.

items.evidence_note: Step 8 shows the pending configuration with quantity 1. Step 9 shows the same configuration with quantity 2.
items.rationale: The quantity change is reflected in the pending purchase configuration before cart addition.

items.text: The system shall preserve a user-selected digital or mobile ticket fulfillment choice across cart review and the transition into checkout unless the user explicitly changes it.

claims.claim: A digital or mobile ticket fulfillment choice is selected in the purchase flow.
The selected fulfillment choice is preserved across cart review and checkout transition.
Actual cross-step persistence of the fulfillment choice can be verified without hidden state.

items.evidence_note: No explicit digital or mobile ticket fulfillment choice is visible in the provided cart review, and the checkout transition is not shown.
items.rationale: The screenshots do not provide a reliable basis for judging persistence of a fulfillment choice.

items.text: The system shall clearly indicate the downstream delivery destination or channel for digital tickets, such as email or mobile wallet, before the user proceeds to payment.

claims.claim: The purchase flow identifies a downstream delivery destination or channel for digital tickets before payment.
Actual external delivery to the destination or channel is outside the captured purchase flow.

items.evidence_note: The pre-checkout cart is visible, but it does not show an email, mobile wallet, or other digital ticket delivery destination.
items.rationale: The required delivery-channel indication is not visible, and actual delivery would be external to the UI evidence.

items.text: The system shall enforce any required pass-ownership or eligibility policy for park add-ons and explain that policy in the purchase flow before checkout.
items.annotation_notes: The explanatory part is visible, while enforcement of eligibility policy is not verifiable from screenshots alone.

claims.claim: The purchase flow explains pass-ownership or eligibility policy for park add-ons.
The system enforces required pass-ownership or eligibility policy before checkout.
claims.note: It is only shown for the Go-Kart Pass and not for the other add ons. But it is indicated in the top bar of the checkout. There are other passes and Dining options.

items.evidence_note: Steps 6 and 8 disclose membership availability and ride restrictions, but no policy enforcement behavior is demonstrated.
items.rationale: The explanatory part is visible, while enforcement of eligibility policy is not verifiable from screenshots alone.

items.text: The system shall disclose all monetary components that can affect the final pre-checkout charge for the selected park purchase, including any park-specific surcharges or fulfillment-related fees.

claims.claim: The pre-checkout charge disclosure includes monetary components for the selected park purchase.
The disclosed monetary components cover all park-specific surcharges and fulfillment-related fees that can affect the final pre-checkout charge.

items.evidence_note: Step 10 shows subtotal, processing fee, tax, and total, but cannot prove completeness for all possible park-specific surcharges or fulfillment-related fees.
items.rationale: The visible monetary summary is supported, while the universal completeness claim is not settled by the screenshots.

items.text: The system shall provide a dedicated pre-checkout review step where the user can confirm or change the selected ticket fulfillment method before continuing to payment.

claims.claim: The system provides a dedicated pre-checkout review step before payment.
The pre-checkout review step lets the user confirm or change the selected ticket fulfillment method before payment.

items.evidence_note: Step 10 shows the relevant pre-checkout cart review, but no ticket fulfillment method confirmation or change control is present in that review step.
items.rationale: The shown pre-checkout review step visibly lacks the required fulfillment-method confirmation or change mechanism.

items.text: The system shall keep the selected park context, configured add-on quantity, and chosen ticket fulfillment method synchronized between add-on configuration, cart line items, and order summary screens.

claims.claim: The selected park context is synchronized between add-on configuration, cart line items, and order summary states.
The configured add-on quantity is synchronized between add-on configuration and cart line items.
The chosen ticket fulfillment method is synchronized between add-on configuration, cart line items, and order summary states.

items.evidence_note: Park context and add-on quantity are carried through configuration and cart review, but no chosen ticket fulfillment method is visible in those states.
items.rationale: The synchronization requirement is supported for park context and quantity, but missing for ticket fulfillment.
